dish: St. Elmo's shrimp cocktail (the fiery horseradish sauce) and steaks in a less formal room
w: St. Elmo's sister restaurant and next-door neighbour (1997) — an upscale American grill that shares St. Elmo's famous shrimp cocktail and steaks with a broader menu around a lively bar. On Indianapolis Monthly's Swoon List.

dish: St. Elmo shrimp cocktail and filet sliders with Prohibition-era cocktails
address: 127 S Illinois St (2nd floor of St. Elmo Steak House), Indianapolis, IN
w: St. Elmo's upstairs lounge, named for the year Prohibition ended — brick walls, an 1898 back bar, the famous shrimp cocktail and filet sliders with classic cocktails. Indianapolis Monthly's No. 5 best bar.

dish: Wet-aged prime filet with horseradish–bleu cheese crust; Cajun New York strip
address: 47 S Pennsylvania St (Majestic Building), Indianapolis, IN
w: Locally owned steakhouse in the Romanesque Revival Majestic Building, named for its street number — Indianapolis Monthly's 'Indy's Great Steakhouses' pick; WISH has called it Indy's No. 1 steakhouse.

dish: Craft cocktails and chef Craig Baker's shareable small plates over Monument Circle
address: InterContinental Indianapolis (11th floor), Market St at Monument Circle, Indianapolis, IN
w: Indoor-outdoor rooftop lounge on the 11th floor of the InterContinental (opened Feb 2025) — Indy's highest bar, looking straight down on Monument Circle; Axios called it the star of the city's rooftop-bar lineup.

dish: Steaks and seafood in Indiana's only revolving rooftop dining room
address: Hyatt Regency Indianapolis (rooftop), 1 S Capitol Ave, Indianapolis, IN
w: Rotating restaurant atop the 22-storey Hyatt Regency since 1977 — one of fewer than two dozen revolving rooftop restaurants left in North America; 360° views of downtown.

dish: Coastal Italian pastas (clams-and-broccolini linguine); regional Italian wine list
address: 339 S Delaware St (The Alexander hotel), Indianapolis, IN
w: Coastal-Italian dining room in The Alexander hotel from Cunningham Restaurant Group — scratch pasta and one of Indiana's deepest Italian wine lists (Wine Spectator Award of Excellence 2025).

dish: Belgian-style frites and Liège waffles with Taxman's Belgian-style house beers
w: Taxman Brewing's downtown gastropub and beer garden in an 1800s livery building in CityWay — Indiana-beef burgers, Belgian frites, 20 house drafts.

dish: Family-recipe red-sauce Italian (meatballs, lasagna) from a 1930 lineage
w: Revival (2009) of Indianapolis's first full-service Italian restaurant, opened by Santora 'Fred' Iozzo in 1930 — his great-granddaughter cooks the family recipes in a near-south-side room by Lucas Oil Stadium.

dish: Dry-aged Duroc pork chop; the Spoke Burger; barrel-aged cocktails
address: 123 S Illinois St (Le Méridien), Indianapolis, IN
w: Le Méridien's racing-themed, mid-century-modern restaurant and bar — Midwestern comfort food done ambitiously, with barrel-aged cocktails at a brass-edged bar.

dish: House pastas (short-rib spaccatelli); tableside king-crab bisque
address: Hotel Indy, 141 E Washington St, Indianapolis, IN
w: Hotel Indy's 52-seat restaurant named for the Hulman family of the Speedway — chef Patrick Russ (ex-Next, Chicago) makes the pastas and sausages in house; Indianapolis Monthly 3 stars.

dish: Indy-inspired cocktails and Midwest bites on an open-air rooftop
address: Hotel Indy (6th floor), 141 E Washington St, Indianapolis, IN
w: Sixth-floor open-air rooftop bar at Hotel Indy named for racer Erwin 'Cannon Ball' Baker — a slight Art Deco feel and some of the best downtown skyline views.

dish: Smoked prime rib; bison burger with charred-tomato glaze
w: Pre-game tavern a walk from Lucas Oil Stadium and the Convention Center — 12-tap bar, sky-high ceilings and a skyline deck; a chef-driven menu that avoids bar-food clichés.

dish: Sushi and specialty rolls
w: CityWay sushi bar (2024) that Axios checked out on opening and Indianapolis Monthly's Feed flagged — a sit-down sushi option by Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

dish: Quattro Formaggi pie; thin crust with pine nuts, prosciutto and a mozzarella–provolone–pecorino blend
w: Indy's pizza institution since 1986 (Broad Ripple), on Mass Ave since 1989 — 'consistently local pizza lovers' favorite', with a string of Best of Indy titles; named Indiana's best family pizza joint.

dish: Three-meat (sirloin, chuck, brisket) burger; the Bru Burger with taleggio and tomato jam
w: Mass Ave burger bar from Cunningham Restaurant Group — Reader's Digest named it Indiana's best burger; Indianapolis Monthly Best of Indy No. 9.

dish: Achiote-braised pork tacos; 100 tequilas and bourbons
w: Late-night taco-tequila-whiskey bar of timbers, barrels and Edison bulbs — on Indianapolis Monthly's 25 Best Tacos list.

dish: Confessional IPA brewed where the pulpit stood
w: Brewpub inside a 135-year-old former Catholic church — a bar built from old pews and floor joists, the brewhouse where the altar was, award-winning Confessional IPA.

dish: Three generations of family-recipe Italian (lasagna, veal, house sauce)
w: Family-run Italian dining room founded in 1960 by military chef Guerino and on Beech Grove's Main Street since 1962 — one of Indianapolis's best locally owned Italian restaurants.

dish: The Ron Swanson (double bacon, pepperoni, ham, salami) on a fluffy-chewy crust
w: Gothic-muralled Main Street pizzeria with a fluffy-yet-chewy hand-tossed crust; beer comes from the Scarlet Lane taproom next door.

dish: Root beer floats, coney dogs and burgers from carhops
w: 1957 Dog 'n Suds drive-in (The Suds since 1973) keeping its '50s look and menu — open April to October, with Saturday cruise-ins of 200–300 classic cars; Car Craft named it a top-five US drive-in.

dish: Laphet thoke (tea-leaf salad); mee goreng
w: Little-Burma counter on the Madison Ave corridor — tea-leaf salad and a light, flavorful Malaysian-style mee goreng; an Indianapolis Monthly Swoon List and best-appetizers pick.

dish: Pork with pickled mango; Burmese curries and breakfast
w: Greenwood Burmese kitchen serving Burmese breakfast, curries and pork with pickled mango to the south side's Chin and Burmese community.

dish: Bone marrow, pig tails and poutine; meatloaf reworked; Bar Rev cocktails in back
w: Progressive American gastropub that 'put Greenwood on the culinary map' in 2014 — ex-Mesh chefs cooking Indiana-raised meat in a historic Old Town building, with the dapper-divey Bar Rev behind. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2018 / 25 Best (No. 24).

dish: Mexico City paletería-style ice cream (guava, tequila); dorilocos; tres leches waffles
w: Mexican-owned Southport-area ice cream and snack parlour bringing Mexico City street sweets and dorilocos to the south side — an Indianapolis Monthly best-snacks pick; on Mirror Indy's best-ice-cream-flavors list.

dish: Chocolate-mint porter, Kanu Bier, Roch Bock
w: Beech Grove's first brewery — a laid-back Main Street taproom with an eight-barrel brewhouse; stars are a chocolate-mint porter and German-style lagers.

dish: Fold-able New York–style slices; pan-baked Grandma pie; garlic knots
address: 8810 S Emerson Ave, Ste 240, Indianapolis, IN
w: South-side New York–style pizzeria — fermented house dough, slices to fold like a New Yorker and a puffy Grandma pie. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2025 and 25 Essential Eats.

dish: Polpo (octopus), mushroom lasagna, tuna crudo
w: 'Next-generation Italian' in Fall Creek Place (the old Shoefly Public House corner) — modern small plates and handmade pasta; voted among Indy's top restaurants.

dish: Tinker Coffee affogato; paninis on Amelia's bread with Smoking Goose meats
address: 236 E 16th St (at Alabama St), Indianapolis, IN
w: Breakfast-and-lunch café and coffee bar in the old Herron School metalworking studio ('the Foundry') — Goose the Market alum Kimmie Burton; jazz nights.

dish: Loose-leaf teas and breakfast; First Friday spoken word
w: Indy's premier tea bar for serious tea drinkers, owned by WNBA great and Fever legend Tamika Catchings — breakfast hours and a First Friday spoken-word series.

dish: Single-sourced Greeley, Colorado corn-fed steaks; the original Glass Chimney bar
w: Glass-walled 9,000 sq ft Carmel steakhouse from the Ritz Charles family, white tablecloths and green velvet, with the bar salvaged from the beloved Glass Chimney. Indianapolis Monthly Best New Restaurants 2019; 'Face of Steaks' 2025.

dish: Fresh seafood and sushi, surf-and-turf
address: 110 W Main St (Sophia Square), Carmel, IN
w: Award-winning surf-and-turf dining room on the ground floor of Sophia Square in Carmel's Arts & Design District, just east of the Monon.

dish: Coastal-California seafood plates
w: Monterey's Fishers sister in the Nickel Plate District — a seafood-heavy, coastal-California room that Visit Hamilton County calls one of Fishers' most sought-after dining destinations.

dish: Omelettes, the Cuban breakfast, cinnamon toast
address: E 116th St (Nickel Plate Trail), Fishers, IN
w: Fishers outpost (2024) of Martha Hoover's Café Patachou — the 1989 Indy breakfast institution Bon Appétit named among the country's top ten breakfast spots — right on the Nickel Plate Trail.

dish: Conch fritters, conch ceviche, peel-and-eat shrimp, smoked fish dip
w: Key West conch house on Zionsville's brick Main Street from restaurateur Shari Jenkins — Cuban, Bahamian and Keys flavours, rare in Indiana.

dish: Pork chop smothered in tomato-bacon jam; fried green tomatoes
w: Steak-and-seafood Americana with two cocktail bars in a repurposed barn on Westfield's Restaurant Row (Nyla and Scott Wolf).

dish: Fish and chips with house tartar; Yorkshire eggs; scones with clotted cream
w: British pub-and-tea-room near Geist doing the standards properly — fish and chips, Yorkshire eggs, cream tea. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2024 & 2025.

dish: Japanese tavern-inspired plates; King Dough 'Final Cut' slices
w: Indy's independent nonprofit art-house cinema and restaurant in Windsor Park — three screens plus a bar-brasserie that switched to a Japanese tavern menu (Axios 2025) and a King Dough slice shop.

dish: Falafel (Axios: some of Indy's best), gyros, baked lamb, spanakopita
w: Greek-Mediterranean kitchen in the old Legend Classic Irvington Cafe space — Axios rates its falafel among the city's best.

dish: Smashed-patty burgers (PBJ Time with honey-roasted peanut butter; Big Kahuna)
w: Irvington smashburger counter that sold out of 500 patties by 6pm on opening day — an Indianapolis Monthly taste-test pick in Indy's smashburger boom.

dish: Cranturkey, Drunkin Radish and Beer and Bacon sandwiches
w: Family-owned Irvington staple — meat-and-cheese counter, local-goods grocery and sandwich shop; an Indianapolis Monthly best-specialty-markets pick.

dish: Burgers, onion rings, flavored Cokes and cinnamon shakes
w: 900 sq ft checkered-floor '50s diner in a 1961 Peppy Grill building — a handful of booths and counter stools facing the flat-top. WRTV historic restaurants that still hold up; IM Cheap Eats.

dish: Tacos and margaritas
w: Fountain Square's beloved family Mexican spot, which closed unexpectedly in early 2025 and rose again in July 2025 on Virginia Ave in Fletcher Place (ground floor of the Slate apartments).

dish: Thai curries and noodle dishes
w: Ed Rudisell's locally owned Thai restaurant in historic Fountain Square, long rated one of Indy's best ethnic restaurants.

dish: Breaded pork tenderloin (outsells everything else four to one)
w: Speedway Main Street grill (Hill family, 2006) a few blocks from the Speedway — its Hoosier breaded tenderloin is the runaway best seller; a race-week institution.

dish: Crêpes, broken-yolk sandwich, the grilled cheese Axios calls perfect; Champagne by the glass
w: Martha Hoover's (6× James Beard semifinalist restaurateur) French neighbourhood bistro and Champagne bar in Broad Ripple — Zagat/Travel + Leisure top-10 US spots for iconic French food.

dish: Homemade meatballs, steamed mussels, lasagna
w: Italian institution in a 1920s stucco house with a romantic terrace on 54th Street — Indianapolis Monthly 25 Essential Eats and FOX59's 'one of Indy's best'.

dish: 40+ regional craft taps incl. house Twenty Below beers; soy-glazed pork belly, poutine
w: SoBro craft-beer pub with a 40-plus regional tap rotation and its owner's own Twenty Below brewery beers; reopened after a 2023 fire.

dish: Blistered Neapolitan-style pies from a brick oven
w: Martha Hoover's 2011 Neapolitan pizzeria at 49th & Pennsylvania, around the corner from the original Café Patachou — Indianapolis Monthly 25 Best Restaurants (No. 22). The Fashion Mall branch closed June 2026; this flagship stays open.

dish: Shrimp pil pil with chermoula; lamb shank tagine with apricots and almonds
w: French-Moroccan dining room and cocktail lounge in the old Sinking Ship dive bar (fall 2025) — Casablanca-born, French-trained chef Aziz Mountassar; its lamb tagine is already among the city's best lamb dishes (Indianapolis Monthly).

dish: Deli sandwiches and bakery case, Butler-Tarkington since 1979
w: Butler-Tarkington bakery-deli-café and community hangout since 1979 — taken over in August 2025 by a lifelong regular determined to keep it as it was.

dish: Cupcakes, with the most vegan and gluten-free options of the chain
w: Indiana's original cupcake bakery (Kate Drury, 2007) — the Illinois Street first shop carries the most vegan and gluten-free choices; an Indianapolis Monthly Great Bakes pick.

dish: Lattes and specialty drinks from a walk-up/drive-thru at Fall Creek and College
w: Locally owned Mapleton-Fall Creek coffee shop (Danny Heller, 2020) on the corner of College Ave and Fall Creek Parkway — grew a second shop on Monument Circle.

dish: Metal-band-named burgers and craft beer
w: Chicago's heavy-metal burger bar on the corner of Morris and Prospect — its first location outside Chicago; reopened after a fire.

dish: Southwest-leaning brunch plates and vegan brunch options
w: Scruffy rock-star diner from Hi-Fi/MOKB's Josh Baker in the historic G.C. Murphy Building, next to the Hi-Fi music venue — morning-to-night brunch with Southwestern flavours.

dish: Double-bone pork chop with apple-bourbon reduction; Chicken à la Marco
address: Delaware St (former Regions Bank by Riley Towers), Indianapolis, IN
w: Old-school Italian-American-meets-steakhouse (2025) from FortyFive Degrees/Metro owner Bill Pritt in a former bank, its drive-thru reborn as a terrace.

dish: Black & Blue flatbread, gumbo, fried goat cheese salad; cocktails facing the 1879 courthouse
w: Upscale, speakeasy-tinged room on Noblesville's courthouse square — sushi, sliders, flatbreads and an 8-oz filet.

dish: Omakase nigiri flights; A5 Miyazaki wagyu
address: The Farm at Silo Crossing, Zionsville, IN
w: Chef Aziz Mountassar's (Marrakesh) omakase room in Zionsville — Japanese cuisine with French technique and Moroccan/Italian accents.

dish: Lift Off IPA
w: Craft brewery on two acres off Speedway's Main Street in view of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway — award-winning Lift Off IPA, concerts, pizza and a dog-friendly yard.

dish: House-rubbed smokehouse barbecue, raw-bar oysters, 750+ bourbons
n: Doc Crow's Southern Smokehouse and Raw Bar
address: 130 S Pennsylvania St (Hyatt Place), Indianapolis, IN
w: Louisville's 16-year-old smokehouse-and-raw-bar opened its first Indiana outpost (May 2025) in the Hyatt Place across from Gainbridge Fieldhouse, in the old Pier 48 space — dry-rubbed barbecue and one of downtown's deepest bourbon walls.

dish: All-you-can-eat churrasco carved tableside
address: 1001 N State Rd 135 (Meridian Meadows), Greenwood, IN
w: Locally owned Brazilian churrascaria (opened March 2025) that an opening-night guest told Indianapolis Monthly rivals Fogo de Chão and Terra Gaucha.
